purpose: B3 of the build capability plan (2026-11-14): observe a live repair round on a fair task. Every rule is stated in the spec; several (half-up rounding, line numbering that counts blank and comment lines, a trailing \r, first-record spelling, lowercased tie order, +5 as an invalid score) are easy to miss on a first draft. One visible case (A1.2, an average of 82.25) fails for the usual binary floating point or round() draft, so the repair feedback can show expected against actual output
declared_scale: One module (src/main.py), one builder task, 4 automated checks, 10 frozen studio cases of which 6 are held out, plus 22 extended held-out cases scored after the build

expected_requests.note: Each round is one builder and one reviewer request; each repair round adds two. A repair round is what this benchmark observes, but it is measured, not required (owner decision D)

expected_cost_usd: 0.00 on a plan-backed route (plan_roles). Any metered route is out of this packet
one_run_per_attempt: Each attempt gets its own run, selection, spec and product, so the per-run request cap (30 on the dev studio connection) is never the limit. The spec typed into each run must pass compare-spec
result_when: Recorded as k of 3 attempts verified, and r of 3 attempts that used at least one repair round, with each repair's cause (failed visible case, failed held-out case, reviewer finding or refused patch) and whether the next round fixed it. If no attempt needs a repair, that is the result (owner decision D, 2026-11-14); nothing is re-run to get one
repair_observed_when: An attempt's build folder has round 1 or later with a candidate that was reviewed and tested, after round 0's candidate failed a case or got a review finding (not only a refused patch). The Build page timeline of that build shows the round and the Why did it fail? panel of the stopped round
invalid_attempt_when: An infrastructure fault outside the roles (worker crash, studio restart, plan outage) stops the attempt before a verdict. It is recorded with its cause, and each attempt may be replaced at most once
refused_patch_rule: A patch the studio's patch contract or scoped tool refuses changes nothing and counts as one repair round (within max_repairs 2 and max_calls 6). It is recorded as a refusal, not as an observed repair
scorer_fault_rule: If the studio verified the build but exporting or scoring fails for an infrastructure reason (Bubblewrap missing, a path problem, a scorer crash), the same exported package (same product_tree_sha256) may be exported or scored again. That does not re-run any role. A grader result on a package is final once it is produced
ordering_note: The expected outputs were written by the author from the spec rules and then checked against the reference solution; the spec, cases and reference were written in the same commit (B3 branch), before any studio or model run
pass_bar_per_attempt: Studio build reaches verified_candidate: QA passes 10 of 10 frozen build cases, including 6 of 6 held out, in the WSL2 isolation worker, and the reviewer approves with no findings (the studio's own rule)
Requests used are at most the plan's max_calls (6)
compare-spec passes for the stored spec
The exported package scored by the frozen grader passes 10 of 10 build cases and 22 of 22 extended cases
measure_and_record: requests used and repair rounds used, and for each repair round its cause and whether it fixed it
patches refused at admission, with each refusal's reason (refused-N.json)
wall time from Start to verified or stopped
reviewer verdict and findings per round (verbatim summary)
QA pass counts per round, development and held out
compare-spec result for the stored spec
grader JSON (freeze_sha256, grader_sha256, product_tree_sha256, build, extended, resources)
clean export start: the exported package, extracted outside the studio, runs under the grader with no studio files present
plan daily request count before and after

known_failure_cases.description: Average formatted from binary floating point ('%.1f' % (total / count))
Average rounded with Python's round(), which rounds halfway values to even
Line numbers count records only, not blank and comment lines
A trailing \r is kept, so a CRLF score is invalid
Names printed in the last record's spelling
Ties ordered by the printed name (uppercase first) instead of the lowercased name
Scores parsed with int(), so +5 is accepted
A record split on its last comma, so a name may hold commas

limits_found_while_freezing: A studio build runs at most 10 cases per task (MAX_BUILD_CASES), so the easy-to-miss rules are spread over 6 held-out studio cases and 22 extended cases
No case can force a repair: a careful first draft passes everything, which is a valid result
